title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 214
summary: Build 214 makes Add a Server a real installation marketplace. Every card that says it installs was installed for real on a test PC before it shipped, and the ones that can't work yet say why instead of pretending.
changes: **13 more game servers**, each installed and started for real on Windows: ARK: Survival Evolved, ARK: Survival Ascended, Space Engineers, Core Keeper, V Rising, Enshrouded, Unturned, Satisfactory, Don't Starve Together, 7 Days to Die, Garry's Mod, Project Zomboid and Factorio (Factorio on Linux). Cards name the operating systems they were tested on; untested ones say so.

**Databases, apps and media as Docker services:** PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Redis, Grafana, Prometheus, Uptime Kuma, Gitea, Nextcloud, Nginx, Jellyfin (with a read-only media folder), Immich (as one Compose project), IT-Tools and Stirling PDF. Passwords are generated per install and shown once; AnxOS keeps no copy. Utilities are published on this computer only by default.

**Deploy your own application:** a Java .jar, or a zipped Node.js or Python project, runs as a managed app with start, stop, logs and resource use. The archive is checked before anything is created. AnxOS does not install npm or pip packages yet: bring node_modules with a Node.js project; a Python project that lists packages is refused with a message.

**Discord.js Bot** deploys your own zipped bot. Its bot token is stored encrypted by the AnxOS Agent and given to the bot as DISCORD_TOKEN when it starts; it is never saved in the bot's files or shown again.

**Server secret store.** Passwords a server needs at start (Project Zomboid's administrator, a bot token) are stored encrypted by the Agent, separately from the server's settings, files and backups, and removed from its console output.

**Modrinth modpacks install and run.** Every Modrinth pack failed with "server-pack runtime could not be resolved" since Build 193; AnxOS now installs the Minecraft and loader version the pack declares.
**Minecraft servers on Windows PCs that have their own Java installed** could fail to start ("executable is outside approved paths"); AnxOS's bundled Java is now chosen.
**Python apps on Windows** were never detected (the "python3" command there is the Microsoft Store shortcut).
**Windows game servers started by name** ("not found") and **UDP-only servers stuck on Starting**, including Valheim, Palworld and V Rising, now start and report ready.
**Minecraft Bedrock (Docker)** installs again; it needs the Minecraft EULA, which the wizard now asks for, and keeps its world.
**Settings files are escaped:** a quote or angle bracket in a server name can no longer add settings to a game's settings file.

**Docker:** busy ports are detected before anything is created, slow image downloads and container starts no longer fail as "Agent unavailable", and the volume list loads on computers with many containers.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 213
summary: Build 213 is about running more than one computer. You can see every computer's servers in one list, keep Agents up to date from the app, move a server between computers, and run AnxNet's relay and gateway on a server you own.
changes: **All computers in My Servers.** One list of every server on every computer, with the computer each one runs on. Start, stop or restart several at once; stop and restart ask first. A computer that is offline keeps its servers listed as "last known".

**Update Agents from the app.** Agent Control can update Linux computers whose Agent was installed from the `anxos-agent` package, one at a time or all together. Each package is checked against the release's checksums first, and if the new Agent doesn't come up, the previous one is put back. An update is refused while that computer's servers are running.

**Automatic Agent updates (off by default).** Settings > Updates > Automatic Agent updates: choose which computers, which days and what time window, and whether AnxOS only tells you or installs the update. Every update is listed in its history. It never restarts an Agent while its servers are running.

**Safer moves between computers.** Before a server moves, AnxOS checks that the target is online, the server is stopped, the platform matches and there is room (ports, memory, disk, size). It won't start while a check fails. The backup is verified before it is sent and checked again when it arrives. After a clean move, AnxOS offers to switch over to the new copy.

**Modpack updates.** Servers installed from a Modrinth or CurseForge modpack say when a newer version of the pack exists for the same Minecraft version and loader. AnxOS tells you; it doesn't apply the update yet.
**Download server files from your phone.** Phone Access can download any file in a server's folder, byte for byte.

**AnxNet edge on your own server.** The AnxNet panel has **Copy edge config**, the edge checks its settings before it starts, and a step-by-step guide covers running it as a service (`docs/ANXNET_EDGE_DEPLOYMENT.md`).
**A colourful Agent screen** on Linux computers without a desktop.

**Cancelling a server update before SteamCMD starts now stops it.** Before, a Cancel during the pre-update backup, or while the update waited for another SteamCMD task, was acknowledged but the update could still run afterwards. With an Agent older than Build 213, the app offers Cancel only once SteamCMD is running and says why.
**The phone no longer opens binary files as text.** Tapping a `.jar` or an image opened it in the editor, where saving could have damaged it.
**The AnxNet edge refuses unsafe settings**, such as a public port range that includes SSH or the Agent's port, or a gateway without a public address.
**The Download Manager no longer shows "cancelled"** for an operation it couldn't stop.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 212
summary: Build 212 is a stability and security release. It fixes 143 defects found in a full review of the app, the Agent, Sharing and AnxNet. The only additions are recovery controls for problems it now detects.
changes: **Restore AnxOS Helper.** If an update could not set the Helper up again (for example, the administrator prompt was declined), the app says so and restores it with one click.
**Approve a changed SSH host key** from the app instead of the connection staying blocked.
**AnxNet shows when its identity is locked** (its key could not be read) instead of silently creating a new one.
**Crash-loop protection** stops restarting a server that keeps crashing within ten minutes of starting, after three tries.
**Servers that are running but not ready** now raise a degraded alert.
**Stop on Windows** asks the server to shut down and save before forcing it.

**Remote Agents can no longer be taken over from the network.** Pairing and enrollment accept only the full Agent credential, not a short fingerprint of it. A freshly paired computer is protected at once instead of after its next restart. A computer you removed can only be paired again from that computer itself.
**The Agent limits what an unauthenticated caller can make it do** (request sizes are capped).
**This PC's Agent credential is never sent to another computer**, and node-credential recovery can no longer save it as a remote computer's credential.
**A file dropped on the window can no longer replace the app.**

**An interrupted restore never leaves a server deleted.** A full restore, and the rollback after a failed one, build the restored copy beside the server and swap it in. If the Agent stops in the middle (an update, a restart, a crash), it puts the server back when it starts again. Agent shutdown also waits for a running restore.
**Updating AnxOS keeps the AnxOS Helper.** If Setup cannot set it up again (for example, the administrator prompt is declined), the app offers **Restore AnxOS Helper**.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 211
summary: Build 211 is the first public build since Build 209. It adds an **optional AI assistant** (off by default) and a **signed, branded Windows installer that works with Smart App Control on**. It also includes every Build 210 improvement; Build 210 was never published.
changes: **Optional AI assistant (Phase X).** An Owner can turn it on in **Settings › AI Assistant**; until then nothing about it runs.
**Branded AnxLabs installer.** A dark AnxLabs installer that explains each choice, including whether to set up the background Helper. Add/Remove Programs lists the publisher as AnxLabs.
**Status explanations and remembered filters.** Hover a server's status to see what it means and what to do next. The Instances status filter is remembered.

**Works with Smart App Control on.** Every program file Windows checks is now signed, including the installer's own helper files and native modules. The signed release candidate installed, ran, reinstalled and uninstalled in a clean Windows with Smart App Control on, with no blocks.

**Updates are checked before they open.** A downloaded update installer must carry a valid signature from the AnxOS publisher, or it is not opened. Settings › Updates shows what was verified, and why an install was refused.
**Errors stay up long enough to read**, and the Docker page, installs, consoles, Instances, Dashboard and Files do much less background work.
**Docker start, stop and restart from the Agent** failed because the Docker path was passed incorrectly.
**Palworld cards showed "0.0" as the game version.**
**Restoring an imported world backup could delete the whole server folder.** World restores now touch only the world folders and refuse archives that hold anything else.

**New downloads may show a SmartScreen prompt** until this release builds download reputation. The installer is validly signed; choose **More info › Run anyway** only if the publisher shown is Anjo ROSIMO.
**Upgrading from Build 209 with Smart App Control on** was not tested in a clean machine; fresh installs, reinstalls and uninstalls were.

**AI assistant:** off by default. Player ping, server TPS and internet reachability are not measured, and it says so. It does not change ports. Sona is not available yet. Its fixes for comparing computers and matching partial computer names were verified in tests and in the app, not yet re-run against a real remote fleet.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 210
summary: Build 210 was not published on its own. Its changes ship in Build 211: status explanations, a remembered Instances filter, readable error messages, much less background work, and the Palworld version fix.
changes: **Status explanations.** Hover a server's status (Running, Stopped, Setup Required, Failed and others) to see what it means and what to do next. When an action failed, the tooltip still shows that error instead.
**Remembered Instances filter.** The status filter on the Instances page is kept between sessions on this computer.

**Errors stay up long enough to read.** Error messages now stay about 6.5 seconds and warnings about 4.5 seconds, instead of 2.2. Hovering keeps them up, and clicking one opens it in Notifications. Other messages are unchanged and never block clicks.
**Faster searching in Settings and Diagnostics.**
**Less background work while you use the app.**
**Clearer app description.** Installers and the Linux app menu now describe the app as managing home servers, game servers, and the computers that run them.

**Palworld cards showed "0.0" as the game version.** Servers installed before Build 209 kept a "0.0" placeholder written by older version detection. "0.0" is no longer accepted as a version, and saved records are detected again once, so the placeholder is dropped. The Steam build number is kept.
None recorded yet.

**Repository validation (source, before the release candidate):** `npm run rc:validate`, 366 of 366 suites, on Windows. That run set the packaged hardware-telemetry helper aside, because the service-managed Agent test fixture counted the Agent's own temperature sampler as an unexpected launch. The fixture now lists the sampler as a background helper, so the suites pass with the helper present.
**Signed CI build, upgrade and acceptance:** not yet run. Results are recorded here before publication.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 209
summary: Build 209 adds a **Sign in** button for game servers that need an account sign-in and fixes Hytale's status reporting. It also adds automatic server update checks with backups and rollback, Discord/webhook alerts, and a Mod Manager for Minecraft servers.
changes: **Sign in for game servers (Hytale first).** While a running server needs an account sign-in, its instance page shows **Sign in**.
**Server updates.**
**Restart schedules** use a single dialog and can be edited.
**Server alerts:** each node can post crashes, scheduled restarts and updates to a Discord or HTTPS webhook. The webhook URL stays on the Agent and is never shown again.
**Mod Manager for Minecraft.** A **Mods** tab (**Plugins** on Paper/Purpur) searches Modrinth for the server's version and loader.
**Hytale showed "ready" about 6 seconds early on restarts.** When it restores a saved sign-in, Hytale reports success before it opens its port. "Ready" now waits for the server to finish booting.
**Hytale stayed "ready" after a console `auth logout`.** It now shows as needing sign-in again.
**A sign-in code could be saved without its expiry time,** because two status updates finished out of order. They now happen in order.

**Hytale showed a false "Update available".** Version detection read the Minecraft-style "version" from Hytale's logs and recorded 0.7.5 as "1.0". Hytale's version now comes from its own boot line, which also stays correct after Hytale updates itself. Other non-Minecraft games no longer get a Minecraft version at all. That parsing was also the source of labels like "Minecraft 0.0 - Palworld".
**The instance header said "Ready" after any finished action,** including a successful Stop. It now shows the server's real state.
**Agents:** update node Agents (Agent `.deb` for packaged nodes, Update Agent for desktop-installed user services). Sign-in, Hytale status, update checks and alerts run in the Agent.
**Updating or restarting an Agent stops every server it runs.** Stop them first and back up worlds, then start them again afterwards.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 208
summary: Build 208 adds the official Hytale dedicated server and checks whether AI services actually work, not only whether they run. It also includes Sona as the officially supported AnxLabs AI app and keeps Palworld on the current Steam client library after updates.
changes: **Hytale dedicated server (Linux nodes).** The Marketplace installs Hypixel Studios' official server.

**Health vs Function in the Infrastructure Inventory (AIM-2).** A new Function column shows whether an AI service actually works, next to whether it is running. A service that hasn't been checked shows "Not checked" and is never green.
**Sona is the officially supported AnxLabs AI app.**
**Discontinued integrations.** Open WebUI, Open Terminal and ANX-CorTex no longer appear in AI service diagnostics. Nothing on your machines was removed.
**Palworld kept loading an old Steam client library after updates.** Palworld's launcher copies `steamclient.so` only when the copy is missing, so updated servers kept running an outdated library.
**Network inventory** now says when the netstat fallback could not read a protocol, instead of returning a silently incomplete list.
**Installed Marketplace servers were labelled as Minecraft.** An installed Hytale server's card read "Minecraft 0.7.5". The card now names Minecraft only for Minecraft servers.

**Installed servers showed as "Available" in the Marketplace.** When the Marketplace was the first page opened, either in its own window or after a restart, installed templates weren't recognised. The Marketplace now loads the node's servers when it opens.
**Agents:** update node Agents (Agent `.deb` for packaged nodes, Update Agent for desktop-installed user services). Hytale's status and Palworld's library refresh run in the Agent.
**Functional checks:** off by default. To enable one, add an approved scope to `%APPDATA%\AnxHub\config\functional-probe-scopes.json`. See `docs/v2/AIM2_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD.md`.
**Repository validation:** `npm run rc:validate`, 355 of 355 suites.
**Signed CI build:** Authenticode signature valid and timestamped, SHA-256 recorded, and the update manifest matches the installer.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 207
summary: Build 207 makes AnxOS behave like a proper server app across several machines.
changes: nodes stay reachable through SSH tunnels and Tailscale fallbacks;
every node's Agent can be started, stopped and restarted from Control Center, and only on the machine AnxOS has verified;
passphrase-protected SSH keys work for background tasks through the system SSH agent;
connection blips no longer flash nodes offline;
Playit is set up by linking an account instead of pasting an address;
the desktop app is reorganized, animated and lighter on the GPU.
**Agent Start, Stop and Restart for remote Linux nodes.** Agent Control now controls remote Agents, not only this PC's.

**Verify Access before Agent control.** SSH Start, Stop, Restart and Agent Update stay disabled until a read-only access check passes for the node and its SSH profile. The check signs in, confirms the machine reached is that node, finds the Agent service and checks passwordless control.

**Protection against controlling the wrong machine.** Every SSH Agent action and Agent Update first confirms that the machine reached is the node: its Agent's device ID, or its hostname when the Agent is stopped. If it isn't, nothing runs.
**SSH keys with passphrases for background tasks.** A key profile can use the system SSH agent (on Windows, the OpenSSH Authentication Agent; load the key once with `ssh-add`).

**App-managed SSH tunnels for nodes.** A node whose Agent listens only on the node itself (for example `127.0.0.1` on a VPS) can be reached through an SSH tunnel that Control Center opens, watches and reconnects with backoff. Tunnels use key authentication and a host key you have already approved; they never prompt or accept an unknown key.

**Route fallback with Tailscale suggestions.** A node can have up to four extra addresses. Control Center uses the first one whose Agent proves the paired device identity, so a different machine answering on an address is never trusted. "Find Tailscale route" suggests the node's tailnet address from `tailscale status` (read only).

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 206
summary: Build 206 adds **service-managed instances**: the Agent can now observe and control an existing OS service (a systemd unit) without ever owning its process. The first use is adopting a production FiveM server that already runs as `anxrp-fxserver.service`, without any risk of the Agent launching a second copy.
changes: Package: `AnxOS-Agent-2.0-build206.deb`, SHA-256 `59842c83fd66d98084d991cd7d9769ef1e21f26d71dabd695049770394cb979f`, built on Linux from the LF-exact archive of `cc862de` with only `release.json` changed to build 206 in the build copy.
The official Build 205 package (SHA-256 `7b9410c0433332d30ebb0d8a0b73aed36902f30063ec36d74403e20e60357acd`) is kept on that host as the rollback artifact.

That host's Agent must **not** be self-updated or upgraded until an official release containing this change exists. The official Build 206 package supersedes it. It is **not** identical: it adds the service operations layer (PR #2: `serviceManagedOperations.js`, the operations routes, `safe-restart` on the lifecycle permission tier, `systemctl show --timestamp=unix`), carries official provenance, and no longer ships a stray `ssh2/lib/protocol/crypto/build/` directory that the temporary package picked up from the build host. Both share the dpkg version string `2.0-build206`, so move a host from one to the other with `dpkg -i` (a same-version reinstall); `apt` will report it as already installed. Either way only the Agent service restarts; a managed service such as FXServer is never restarted by the package.

**Service-managed instances (`type: "systemd-service"`).** systemd stays the single owner of the process. The Agent runs only `[sudo -n] systemctl start|stop|restart <unit>` and `systemctl show`; it never spawns, signals or adopts the workload and holds no PID for it. Unreadable service state is shown as Unknown, never Stopped, and lifecycle actions refuse to act on it.

**Operator-authored and allowlisted.** The record is written on disk by an operator and cannot be created or edited through the API. The unit must also be listed in `AGENT_SYSTEMD_UNIT_ALLOWLIST` in the root-owned Agent environment file, and control is limited to exact commands pinned by a sudoers drop-in. See `docs/SERVICE_MANAGED_INSTANCES.md`.

**Desktop support.** Control Center shows these instances as "systemd service" / "Managed by systemd" with a notice naming the unit, a readable reason for Unknown and Failed states, and disables (with an explanation) everything the Agent refuses: console commands, force-kill, editing, renaming, duplicating, deleting, backups and scheduled restarts.
**Capability report.** The Agent health response gains an additive `serviceManagedInstances` capability listing the allowed units.

**Service operations layer (second Build 206 pass).** For a service-managed instance the Agent can now read, without owning anything: systemd's MainPID and uptime, AnxRP health (READY, version, boot id, sessions) from its status file, the connected player **count** from FXServer's loopback `/dynamic.json` and `/players.json` (names and identifiers are never stored or logged), the listening game ports from `/proc/net`, and an optional operator-written deployment manifest (unofficial-build flag, rollback artifact and backup status). New Agent environment variable: `AGENT_SERVICE_STATUS_ROOTS`.

**Safe Restart.** One guarded action that automates the proven Phase 5 flow: verify the instance, unit and MainPID, systemd health, AnxRP READY (fresh) and 0 players, writable history; re-check players; issue **exactly one** `systemctl restart` (never retried); wait for a new MainPID, the listening ports, AnxRP READY with a **new boot id**, and a settle window with no automatic restart. Anything unknown, unreadable or ambiguous refuses or fails closed. Plain start, stop and restart are locked while it runs.

**Restart history.** An append-only `service-history.jsonl` records every Safe Restart (started, then finished), every refusal and every plain start, stop and restart; interrupted operations are detected. A restart is refused if the history cannot be written.

**Control Center.** A SYSTEMD MANAGED badge and operations panel (MainPID, uptime, AnxRP state and boot id, players, ports, preflight checklist, progress, result, history, unofficial-build warning, rollback artifact and backup status, read-only journal in the Console tab) and a specific reason on every disabled control.

**Port-conflict check failed open.** The start preflight ignored listening sockets whose owner it could not identify (for example a server running as another user), counted a process owned by another user as dead, and swallowed errors from the check as "no conflict". Unknown owners and unreadable socket tables now block the start for every instance type.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 205
summary: Build 205 makes the Agent usable on a headless server and brings the same Agent runtime to every surface: the Control Center Agent Control GUI, the `anxos-agent` CLI/TUI, and the Control Center protocol/API. Pairing, identity, authentication, and lifecycle logic keep one authoritative implementation, and the safety defaults that protect a reachable Agent are unchanged.
changes: **Headless Agent CLI/TUI.** A Linux server with no desktop can install the Agent and manage it from the terminal. Running `anxos-agent` opens the TUI, with subcommands for `status`, `pair`, `service status|start|stop|restart`, `logs`, `diagnostics`, `update --check`, `unpair`, `--help`, and `--version`.

**Official Agent package.** `AnxOS-Agent-<version>.deb` for Debian 11+/Ubuntu 22.04+ x64 (glibc >= 2.28), installed as the `anxos-agent.service` systemd system unit, with an `AnxOS-Agent-<version>.deb.sha256` checksum file published alongside the package in `sha256sum -c` format so the download can be verified before install.
**Add Computer, redesigned.** Adding a computer now offers both paths — a desktop computer or a headless server — with the instructions and pairing steps for each, instead of a single ambiguous flow.
**Pairing friction.** The headless path no longer requires a source checkout or developer commands; pairing uses a one-time code from the TUI or `anxos-agent pair`, entered under Add Computer.

**Honest status on headless nodes.** Status, logs, and diagnostics come from the same runtime as the desktop surfaces, so a headless Agent reports the same state the GUI would show instead of a reduced summary.

**Headless pairing presentation.** The Agent CLI/TUI now shows the full pasteable pairing code — with the short `ANX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` kept separately as a reference code — exactly as Control Center redeems it, closing the golden-path gap where the short reference code alone was rejected as invalid.

**Marketplace dependency recovery.** Structured Marketplace errors now cross the Control Center IPC bridge intact (`code`, suggestion, and `details.missingDependencies` are preserved), so the "prepare node / missing Java" recovery path is offered instead of dead-ending.

**Minecraft defaults and honest install outcomes.** Minecraft templates now default to a Java-21-compatible version (1.21.11); Paper/Vanilla pre-flight refuses a version that needs a newer Java with a clear required-vs-available message; and an install whose started process crash-loops now fails honestly (`START_FAILED`) instead of reporting Complete.

**Package upgrade applies immediately.** Upgrading the Agent `.deb` now best-effort restarts the running service (`systemctl try-restart`) so the new payload takes effect without a manual restart; fresh installs are unchanged.

**Safety defaults are unchanged.** The Agent binds loopback (`127.0.0.1`) by default; enabling another computer to connect is an explicit opt-in. While a reachable Agent is not yet paired, anyone who can reach it could claim it, so pair promptly.

Pairing codes are one-time and valid for 10 minutes. Full tokens never appear in the UI, logs, or diagnostics; no authentication, authorization, loopback, or redaction check was weakened in this build.
Supported headless platforms: Debian 11+ and Ubuntu 22.04+ x64 with glibc >= 2.28. Other distributions and architectures are not supported.

title: AnxOS Control Center v2.0 — Build 204
summary: Build 204 is a Private Alpha channel release focused on first-run reliability, safer networking defaults, and stronger recovery safeguards. New installs are guided from download to first server, the Agent stays local to this computer unless you opt in, and the status you see matches what the app is actually doing.
changes: **First-run setup opens on a new install.** The welcome screen and the full setup wizard now appear as expected, so a fresh install is guided through choosing an owner, connecting an Agent, preparing the node, and creating a first server instead of stopping on a blank step.

**The Agent is local-only by default.** The standalone Agent binds to this computer only. Connecting other machines is a deliberate opt-in with a clear startup message, and using a concrete address adds a stricter host check.

**Remote and phone workflows.** Push the bundled Agent runtime to a remote node over SSH with a guard that refuses to downgrade a newer Agent, and pair a phone with a node through a QR code and a browser claim page.
**Server provisioning reliability.** FiveM instances are created with the spawn resources they need, and Minecraft/SteamCMD server updates keep their integrity checks.

**Clearer status everywhere.** The node health badge now matches the health card, the Agent status no longer sticks on "Loading", tunnel and service counters agree with the tunnel state, and the setup wizard no longer claims "Ready" when a node cannot be deployed.
**No more dead ends.** Marketplace and Create Server explain the next step instead of stopping, and controls that have nothing to act on are visibly disabled.

**Reliability under failure.** The Docker page recovers from transient failures instead of stalling, workspace refreshes only run for the page you are on, and polling pauses while the window is hidden.

**Safer recovery.** Orphan backup archives are quarantined instead of deleted, irreversible migrations verify a recovery point before rewriting state, and a disposable restore drill now runs as part of the test suite.

**Security hardening.** Installer archive and extraction paths are contained, requests that look like DNS-rebinding attacks are refused, remote Agent updates cannot silently downgrade, and the shipped dependency set has no known advisories.

**Installer and update reliability.** The Windows packaging check now validates the real packaged contents, and the packaged Agent ships its full dependency set so the Agent starts reliably after install.

title: Release Notes — AnxOS Control Center v2.0 build 203
summary: Build 203 ships the V2-A Wave-1 close-out, the first V2-C and V2-D slices, and the authenticated browser management surface. It rides on top of the published Build 202 stable.
changes: Shared instance identity model, authenticated agent enrollment handshake with nonce-protected start/complete/status paths, and fail-closed owner/admin/operator/viewer role enforcement.

Durable per-instance job lifecycle: state machine, idempotency keys, cancellation, audit events, and restart re-observation. A keyed repeat returns the original job; destructive operations are never replayed.
The agent spawn contract is now explicit: `ANXHUB_CONFIG_DIR` is the sole canonical identity source; legacy `%APPDATA%\AnxHub` bindings auto-migrate only during an explicit enrollment handshake.
A Windows/Linux support matrix documents what is tested, partial, and absent per platform.
Docker engine detection with per-prerequisite diagnostics (not installed, permission denied, daemon unreachable, socket access denied).

Container create/start/stop/restart/delete/pull ride the durable V2-A job store — a client restart can no longer orphan an in-flight container operation. Destructive container operations refuse idempotency keys.
A dedicated smoke pins the docker route manifest, capability report, prerequisite classification, and per-platform executable resolution.
Marketplace templates carry opt-in version stamps, sha256 checksums, and provenance (source) fields. Invalid metadata fails closed with distinct codes; the shipped 33-template catalog is unaffected.
Instances carry managed/imported/external ownership. Silent ownership flips are refused; adoption is an explicit one-way transition that stamps `adoptedAt`.
The instance detail panel surfaces ownership; imported and external services show an "Adopt service" action.

The dashboard gains a widget row (servers, remote systems, node health, metrics freshness) with a staleness policy: when the underlying data is not current, tiles show "Checking…" instead of a fake zero.

The agent serves a session-gated, read-only management page at `/api/v1/ui`. Sessions are short-lived (15 min), bounded (16 active), issued in exchange for the existing bearer credential or a one-time bootstrap code, and use HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict cookies scoped to the UI path.

title: Release Notes — AnxOS Control Center v1.9 build 202
summary: Build 202 completes the UX/quality half of the original bug batch whose crash-only half shipped in Build 201. It rides on top of the published Build 201 stable.
changes: A truthful Agent health `mode` derived from the configured API permissions (`read-write` / `read-only` / `no-access`) replaces the hard-coded "read-only" label that misreported write-enabled agents.
A regression smoke locks the health-mode computation against permission shapes (`*`, wildcards, read-only, empty).
A regression smoke for the node-switch reset contract (generation-keyed, unconditional cleanup).
The node selector no longer sticks on "Switching node…" when a switch never completes: the in-progress flag now resets in an unconditional finally-style guard keyed by a switch generation.

The optional AnxOS cloud device-login no longer hard-fails on machines with no default browser: the pending login is kept, `manualOpenRequired` is surfaced, and a manual open/copy-link fallback path is shown. Local control is unaffected.
The versioning smoke's RC-retry provenance scenario is advanced together with each build bump so release metadata checks track the current build.
Full source validation (187 suites) passes before this build is eligible for release-candidate work.
Reused the disposable-sandbox in-place upgrade acceptance pattern proven in the Build 201 cycle.

title: Release Notes — AnxOS Control Center v1.9 build 201
summary: Build 201 ships the crash-only bugfix batch on top of the Build 200 V2 reliability baseline. Scope was intentionally trimmed to stability fixes; the UX/quality follow-ups (browserless device-login fallback, truthful agent health mode label, node-switch reset) are queued for a later build.
changes: An EPIPE-safe console facade centralizes best-effort logging so a closed or broken pipe cannot destabilize the app.
Unreadable or corrupt instance configs now surface as an explicit `Unavailable` instance instead of being silently dropped (honest-state contract).
An actionable `AGENT_AUTH_FAILED` error with Repair / Rotate Token / Pair guidance is raised when the Agent rejects the request token.
Uncaught `EPIPE` from best-effort console writes can no longer crash the app when the write target's pipe is closed (IPC handlers now route logging through an EPIPE-safe console facade).
An unreadable or corrupt instance config is now surfaced as an explicit `Unavailable` instance instead of being silently dropped, restoring the honest-state contract.
The Agent instance-root fallback is now Windows-aware (`%LOCALAPPDATA% \anxos\instances`) and emits a loud diagnostic instead of silently pointing at a stray `/srv/...` path on Windows.
A rejected Agent token on `/api/v1/stats` now returns an actionable `AGENT_AUTH_FAILED` error pointing to Agent Control (Repair / Rotate Token / Pair) instead of a bare unexplained `UNAUTHORIZED`.
Regression smokes cover the EPIPE guard, the unavailable-config surface, and the health/instance behavior that changed.
Two non-`EOL`-normalizing smokes were hardened and the dependency IPC diagnostics stub updated so the full source validation suite passes.
Full source validation must pass before Build 201 is eligible for commit or release-candidate work.

title: Release Notes — AnxOS Control Center v1.9 build 200
summary: Build 200 establishes the V2 Reliability Contract without beginning the wider V2 architecture or feature vision. Build 199 remains the immutable final V1 release.
changes: A focused Build 199 instance-record fixture and deterministic schema 1 to schema 2 migration contract.

Regression coverage for repeated lifecycle cycles, duplicate stops, already-stopped behavior, and stop timeouts.
Interrupted installs are retained with actionable failure evidence instead of being silently deleted during startup recovery.
Stop timeouts no longer leave instance metadata indefinitely in `Stopping`; a process proven alive remains truthfully `Running` with `INSTANCE_STOP_FAILED` details.
The shutdown regression uses an already-authorized absolute executable path, proving the stop path without broadening executable restrictions.
Website and updater download routing now recognize only the canonical `AnxLabs/AnxOS-Control-Center-Releases` repository and reject source, unrelated, malformed, and legacy-owner URLs.
Focused migration, lifecycle, installation recovery, Marketplace retention, IPC error-contract, and authorization smokes cover the Build 200 changes.
Full source validation must pass before Build 200 is eligible for commit or release-candidate work.

title: AnxOS Control Center v1.9 — Build 199 (Final V1 Build)
summary: Final V1 Private Alpha build. Closes the remaining V1-B acceptance evidence gaps: the explicit V1 feature set with maturity labeling, the audit-trail decision record, and a live backup-to-restore round-trip drill on real hardware. Build 200 is reserved for V2 and is intentionally not created.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Documented the explicit V1 feature set: 20 features with Supported/Alpha-form maturity, the unsupported-in-V1 list, and five UI labeling rules for experimental and unsupported features.

Recorded the action-audit-trail decision: V1 relies on operation records, structured IPC logs, and confirmation dialogs; a tamper-evident audit store is deferred to V2 with explicit trigger conditions.
V1-B acceptance gate position upgraded to met (items 1, 4, and 5 closed with dated evidence; item 3 gained live state-contract evidence).

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Closed V1-B acceptance-record gaps for the feature-set/labeling matrix, audit-trail decision, and live backup-to-restore round trip.
Added the two new V1 records to the documentation index so current normative documents stay discoverable.

sections.heading: Validation
items: Live backup-to-restore round trip executed 2026-09-04 on Better MC [FORGE] BMC4 via the packaged v1.9 build against the Anxlab agent: complete backup, restore with confirmation dialog, agent safety snapshot before restore, restart-after-restore verified. Custom-command instances correctly reject world backups with WORLD_PATH_NOT_FOUND.
qa:fast, qa:feature, rc:validate, docs:architecture:smoke, and onboarding:smoke executed for this build.

sections.heading: Known limitations
items: V1-B item 7 (additional-tester feedback / multi-environment Beta regression) remains evidence-pending.
The code-signing certificate expired 2026-09-05 and must be renewed before the next signed release.
Custom-command instances (Terraria, Rust) have no world directory, so world-only backups are unavailable for them; full-instance backups still apply.
